scenes.headline: How a grid of tiny memories recalls
scenes.sub: Nine cells per token, a cell for every new address.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Lattix! Today: how mu Lattice stores thousands of facts in a grid of tiny memories.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Send each token to a 3 x 3 patch of a growing grid, where every cell is its own small delta-rule memory.
scenes.say: Attention keeps everything and pays more as it grows. A recurrent state pays the same but fills up. Mu Lattice keeps many small states, and visits a few.

scenes.title: Two ways to pay for memory

left.title: One fixed state
left.say: Gated DeltaNet keeps one matrix per head. Cheap, but it only holds so much.

right.title: A lattice of states
right.say: The lattice keeps a matrix per cell, created on first write. Each token touches a small patch.

steps.say: Each token's hidden state becomes a two dimensional address, a point on a grid.
A cosine squared bump spreads it over the three nearest cells on each axis. Nine in all.
Each cell holds its own small matrix, created only when something first writes to it.
A query reads its own nine cells, mixed by the bump weights, however much is stored.

parts.note: what the cell would have said, subtracted
parts.say: The cell predicts the value for this key, and writes only the error.

parts.note: a learned decay on the old contents
parts.say: Old contents decay by a learned gate.

parts.note: write strength, times the bump weight
parts.say: The write is scaled by a gate and by the bump weight.

scenes.label: fewer multiply-adds than attention at 131,072 tokens
scenes.note: PAPER.md counts 7,280x by treating a matrix touch as one operation.
scenes.say: In multiply adds, that is about a hundred and fourteen times less work than attention at a hundred and thirty one thousand tokens. Attention still ran faster on the clock.

scenes.label: Bolt-on test cases answered, seed 999
scenes.say: Bolted onto a frozen language model, it got a hundred and twenty two of two hundred. Exactly the facts whose answers it saw in training.

scenes.text: Per-token work stays flat as memory grows, but capacity is still a number you choose before training.
scenes.mark: a number you choose before training
scenes.say: Work per token really is flat. But the grid has edges, set before training. A much bigger capacity, still a choice.
Address, bump, nine cells. Each cell its own memory. Flat work, on a grid with edges.
